scope: Local Blender art comparison. Windows playable hulls remain at round 172.

owner_reply.chat_direction: It's closer and it's improvements, but as long as we can keep going and as long as you can keep finding better ways to match up and make sure things are matching and make improvements and iterate, right? Let's just keep going.

method: Fixed orthographic gallery cameras. Marked 16 interior pixels and eight on each surround. Sampled the first visible opaque mesh face through the complete assemblies. Several marks guided iterations. Straight port registrations use one uniform scale and translation each. One view cannot verify hidden shapes. The supporting drawings are independent illustrations.

trials: Delta: the first outboard door matched the gallery interior marks but missed the port station. Moving it aft exposed blocking drive shrouds and one long keel end face. Split that face into short strips and seat the passenger flank outside the full room depth.

Glacier: removing the aft wall uncovered only part of the room. Sweeping the pier and angling the chamber freed the right side. The split two-shoe threshold removed the overhanging tray but the blade and rim still partly mask the bay.
remaining: Delta: door center still about 13 pixels high in the registered side drawing. The shoulder and cabin windows read differently. The bright streak continues outside toward the illustrated shuttle; its light source is uncertain. The upper branch-deck material still needs work.
Glacier: three of sixteen interior points still hit the rim or its support. The outboard blade overlaps more of the port elevation than in the side study.
